papers.title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations
papers.abstract: Geometric convolutions on Riemannian manifolds depend on the geometry of the underlying domain, making stability under metric perturbations a fundamental question in geometric deep learning. This paper studies this question for parallel transport convolution through methods from differential geometry and analysis. On a fixed compact manifold, we establish that, for a continuous input signal and a continuous reference kernel supported in a sufficiently small normal neighborhood, the convolution output depends continuously in $L^2$ on the Riemannian metric in the $C^2$-topology, under the specified localization and transport-path conventions. The analysis develops perturbation estimates for geodesics, parallel transport, Jacobi fields, and exponential maps, and uses these estimates to compare the transported kernels. A central difficulty is the cut locus, which obstructs uniform comparison of the transport construction over the entire manifold. We address this difficulty by combining uniform estimates away from the cut locus with integral bounds on neighborhoods of arbitrarily small volume, while also controlling the change in the Riemannian volume measure. The resulting qualitative stability theorem connects perturbation theory for Riemannian geometric constructions with the analysis of spatial convolution operators in geometric deep learning.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
papers.abstract: We study nef line bundles on polarized fibrations $(X/C,\bar{H})$, with a fixed nef metrized ample polarization satisfying $H^d=1$, where $d=\dim X$. We prove a quantitative arithmetic height inequality under relative metric positivity, allowing singular arithmetic models and relatively nef adelic bundles. The height deficit defines a local energy. For nef, relatively ample line bundles over finitely generated fields, this energy is bounded below for almost every complex or nonarchimedean local-field realization of fixed polarized global model data, outside one null set common to the entire relative metric class. The results include big non-semiample examples. For ample $L$ and smooth positively curved $\bar{H}$, the complex critical equation is the Calabi--Yau equation; at zero volume, projective bundles recover Donaldson's functional. We also study critical metrics and conjectural canonical heights defined by energy envelopes.

papers.title: Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
papers.abstract: We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(\Omega\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(\Omega\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partial\Omega\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(\Omega\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that \(h\) is Lipschitz, right and left differentiable at every point, of class \(C^1\) on \(\partial\Omega\setminus\Sigma\), and real analytic on \(\{h\neq g\}\setminus\Sigma\), where \(\Sigma=\{\kappa=0\}\) is the zero set of the curvature of \(\partial\Omega\). Also, at each point \(p\in\Sigma\cap\{h\neq g\}\), the two one-sided branches extend real analytically across \(p\). The proof recasts the vertical part near a contact point as a scalar obstacle problem with a possibly degenerate right-hand side, whose model case is \(\Delta v=H\,\id_{\{v>0\}}\) with \(H\ge0\) a polynomial. These results are optimal: for merely smooth data the trace may be discontinuous, while in the real-analytic case there are examples where corners do occur.

papers.title: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
papers.abstract: We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures. Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number

papers.title: A Geometric Calder\'on Problem for Differential Forms
papers.abstract: We establish boundary determination and global partial-data uniqueness for Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential $p$-forms. We derive an explicit recursion for its full symbol and determine the full boundary jet of the metric, modulo conformal gauge in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$. For $p\geq1$, partial data determine metrics that are analytic in the interior and near the measured boundary subset, up to isometry or conformal equivalence. The global uniqueness relies on a new projection-kernel embedding that detects the unobserved boundary through rank loss and small eigenvalues. We also establish global partial-data uniqueness for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature, using elliptic-transport unique continuation and, in the critical dimension, conformal-geodesic coordinates. A Weyl nondegeneracy condition further upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.

papers.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
papers.abstract: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $\lambda$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $\Delta^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.

papers.title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For compact connected submanifolds of dimension $n\geq4$ with spherical free boundary, we prove preservation and convergence to a round hemisphere in a uniquely determined $(n+1)$-plane. To our knowledge, this is the first such convergence theorem for spherical free boundary MCF in arbitrary codimension. The closed theorem requires additional quadratic pinching for $5\leq n\leq7$, and the free boundary theorem for $4\leq n\leq7$. For $n\geq8$, the necessary quadratic bound follows from quadratic convexity. We also establish preservation of ordinary quadratic pinching $|A|^2\leq c|H|^2$ under spherical free boundary flow for $n\ge2$ and $\frac{9}{8n}\leq c\leq\frac{4}{3n}$, including both endpoints.

papers.title: Flexibility for the Monge-Ampere system implies flexibility for isometric immersions into Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that any flexibility result for the Monge-Amp\`ere system implies the corresponding flexibility result for the isometric immersion system, with the same H\"older regularity. We treat the general isometric immersion system, in which both the source and the ambient metrics are arbitrary H\"older regular, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. Combining this implication with existing results for the Monge-Amp\`ere system, we obtain new ${C}^{1,\alpha}$ flexibility statement for isometric immersions with arbitrary source and ambient metrics. To our knowledge, these are the first such results for non-Euclidean ambient metrics.

papers.title: Sharp Partial Regularity of Weakly Pseudoholomorphic Maps Into Projective Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that a weakly pseudoholomorphic $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ map from a real-analytic almost complex $2m$-manifold into a projective algebraic variety has a countably $(2m-4)$-rectifiable singular set. When $m=2$, the singular set is shown to be locally finite. We first establish both conclusions on smooth almost complex domains under the additional assumption that the pullback of the Fubini--Study form is distributionally closed. We then show that this conservation law follows from the Cauchy--Riemann equation alone on real-analytic domains.

papers.title: Gauss--Bonnet theorem for o-minimal surfaces with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between topology and curvature of surfaces definable in an o-minimal structure. Our main result is a Gauss--Bonnet-type formula for closed (not necessarily compact) definable surfaces with finitely many singular points, expressing the Euler characteristic in terms of the total Gaussian curvature, the local densities at the singular points, and the density at infinity. As consequences, we obtain an inequality for definable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities and, for complex algebraic curves, a formula and an inequality relating the Euler characteristic, the total curvature, the multiplicities at the singular points and the degree.

papers.title: Noncollapsing for Curvature Flows with Inhomogeneous Speeds
papers.abstract: We study closed, embedded hypersurfaces in Euclidean space evolving by fully nonlinear curvature flows, whose speed is given by a symmetric, monotone increasing, $1$-homogeneous, positive underlying speed function $F$ composed with a modulating function $\Psi$. Under the assumption that $F$ is convex or inverse-concave and that $\Psi$ satisfies the corresponding structural conditions, we establish exterior noncollapsing estimates for the flow. The main difficulty stems from the nonlinearity of the evolution equation satisfied in the viscosity sense by the exscribed curvature, whereas in previous works it is a solution to the linearized flow. Moreover, in the case where $F$ is inverse-concave, we adopt an argument different from that of Andrews and Langford to treat off-diagonal extrema.

papers.title: Foliations by constant spacetime mean curvature surfaces for asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data sets
papers.abstract: We construct an exhaustive family of constant spacetime mean curvature (STCMC) surfaces for initial data sets close to the anti-de Sitter-Schwarzschild hyperboloid. In particular, we obtain such a foliation as the long time limit of the volume preserving spacetime mean curvature flow starting from the constant mean curvature foliation constructed by Neves-Tian (Geom. Funct. Anal., 2009). As an application, inspired by the definition of STCMC center of mass for initial data sets proposed in the asymptotically Euclidean setting by Cederbaum-Sakovich (Calc. Var. PDE, 2021), we study the center of mass of an asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data set.

papers.title: Compactifying the $G_2'$-Hitchin component via almost-complex curves
papers.abstract: By studying limits of induced metrics of equivariant almost-complex curves in the pseudosphere $\mathbb{S}^{2,4}$, we compactify the $G_{2}'$-Hitchin component.

papers.title: Wei-Norman Factorization of Frenet-Serret equations and the Cardan Lock
papers.abstract: Frenet-Serret equations for particles moving along differentiable curves, in the case of non-constant curvature and torsion, are considered in the framework of the Wei-Norman factorization of the propagator using the Lie algebra of the rotation group. It leads to a system of coupled linear equations that are highly coupled if Euler or Cardan angles are used, but that can be uncoupled if the Cartan basis in the Lie algebra is used, resulting essentially in a Ricatti equation. However, since the rotations algebra is not a solvable algebra, the global Wei-Norman Theorem does not apply and singularities in the solutions of the system of equations appear at certain points, related to the \text{gimbal o Cardan lock}. Notwidthstanding, a detailed study of the limit at these points shows that in most of the cases the propagator is well defined and gimbal lock is avoided.

papers.title: Fibrations and nilpotent collapsing structure
papers.abstract: We construct fiber bundles, singular fibrations, and nilpotent collapsing structures for Riemannian manifolds with lower Ricci curvature bounds under additional geometric assumptions. For every $n$ and $D>0$, there exists $\epsilon(n,D)>0$ such that a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold $M$ satisfying \[ \operatorname{diam}(M)\le D,\qquad \operatorname{sec}_M\ge-1,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_M\ge-\epsilon(n,D) \] admits a finite cover of degree at most $C(n)$ that is a smooth fiber bundle over a nilmanifold. The fibers have finite fundamental group, and the base dimension equals the Hirsch rank of $\pi_1(M)$. If $\pi_1(M)$ is torsion-free, then $M$ itself fibers smoothly over an infranilmanifold with simply connected fibers. We next consider a Gromov--Hausdorff convergent sequence $M_i\to X$ of closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds with uniformly bounded diameter, $\operatorname{Ric}_{M_i}\ge -(n-1)$, and the $(\rho,\delta)$ local rewinding Reifenberg condition, where $\rho>0$ is fixed and $\delta$ is sufficiently small. For all sufficiently large $i$, we construct singular fibrations $\bar{F}_i:M_i\to X$ that are $\epsilon_i$-Gromov--Hausdorff approximations, with $\epsilon_i\to0$, and whose fibers are homeomorphic to infranilmanifolds. Under the same local hypotheses, complete, possibly noncompact manifolds admit nilpotent collapsing structures on their $\epsilon(n,\rho)$-collapsed regions.

papers.title: On pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian metrics
papers.abstract: In our previous work, we studied the squared $L^2$-norm functionals $\mathcal G$ of Gauduchon's torsion $1$-form and $\mathcal F$ of the Chern torsion over the space of all Hermitian metrics with unit volume on a compact complex manifold. We introduced torsion-critical metrics as critical points of $\mathcal F$. In this paper, We prove that a pluriclosed and astheno-K\"ahler metric is torsion-critical if and only if it is K\"ahler. In particular, every compact pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian threefold is K\"ahler. We also give explicit examples and derive geometric consequences under additional curvature assumptions.

papers.title: Real Determinantal and Segre Varieties: Stability and Area Minimization
papers.abstract: We apply Liu's recently introduced moderation criterion to complete the classification of area-minimizing real determinantal varieties and real Segre varieties, thereby settling the remaining cases left open by Pedersen and Kerckhove--Lawlor \cite{Pedersen93,KerckhoveLawlor1999}. In particular, we prove that $C(2,3,1)$ is area-minimizing modulo $2$, resolving the $g=4$, $(m_1,m_2)=(1,1)$ case of the isoparametric focal-cone problem raised by Tang and Zhang \cite{TZ20} and recently revisited by Liu \cite{Liu2026}.

papers.title: Zeros of Pick and Hopf Differentials and Fences of Convex Domains
papers.abstract: We prove that the vanishing order of a Pick or Hopf differential controls the corresponding convex domain through sharp disk comparisons. For a complete hyperbolic affine sphere, Pick vanishing order $m\ge0$ gives normalized projective coordinates in which the domain lies between disks of radii $\sqrt{\cos(\pi/(m+3))}$ and its reciprocal. For a harmonic diffeomorphism to a convex hyperbolic domain with complete $\partial$-energy metric, Hopf vanishing order $m$ gives a disk in the image of radius $\log\cot(\pi/(2(m+2)))$, centered at the image point. Equality characterizes the corresponding regular polygons. For polygonal targets, these comparisons prove the Fence conjecture of Dumas--Wolf and give explicit Hilbert and hyperbolic distance bounds for higher fences. We also construct simple-zero examples showing that these sufficient multiplicity conditions are not necessary.

papers.title: Coupled flows in $G_2$ geometry: preservation, existence and stability
papers.abstract: We study coupled flows on compact manifolds with $G_2$ structures that preserve coassociative submanifolds and $G_2$ instantons as the ambient $G_2$ structure evolves. For coassociatives, we give an explicit example on a torus showing that the Laplacian flow of closed $G_2$ structures coupled to mean curvature flow can fail to preserve coassociativity, even arbitrarily close to a flat structure. We circumvent this by adding a Lie derivative to the ambient equation, using an elliptic correction of minimum $L^2$ norm along the submanifold. We prove short-time existence and uniqueness of the corrected coupled flow from coassociative initial data, without any rigidity assumption. We also prove global existence and smooth exponential convergence for coassociative initial pairs sufficiently close to a torsion-free coassociative pair, with the ambient cohomology class fixed. For instantons, we propose a similar corrected coupled system by adding a torsion term and a nonlocal elliptic correction to Yang-Mills flow along prescribed coclosed ambient $4$-forms. We prove short-time existence and uniqueness of the corrected coupled system for connections nearby an acyclic $G_2$ instanton. We obtain global existence and smooth exponential convergence for the coupled corrected connection flow and the modified coflow of coclosed $G_2$ structures with parameter zero, near a torsion-free structure with an acyclic instanton. We prove a new result on the global existence and smooth exponential convergence near a torsion-free $4$-form in a fixed cohomology class for the modified coflow with $c=0$ which is a result of independent interest. We also give continuation criteria for both the coupled systems and construct compact examples with nonzero correction. Finally, for every positive coflow parameter, we exhibit a flat torus with a growing linear mode which shows why $c=0$ is the meaningful one.

papers.title: Rigidity for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional in dimensions greater than four
papers.abstract: We investigate rigidity properties of critical metrics for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional on Riemannian manifolds of dimension greater than four. This functional is the integral of the squared norm of the Riemann curvature tensor. On noncompact manifolds, criticality is understood with respect to compactly supported variations, without assuming finite total curvature energy. We prove that every complete noncompact critical metric with finite curvature energy is either flat or has strictly negative scalar curvature everywhere. We further show that every complete critical metric with concircular scalar curvature is flat. Here concircularity means that the Hessian of the scalar curvature is pointwise proportional to the metric. Consequently, every complete weakly Einstein critical metric with divergence-free Cotton tensor is flat. The latter two flatness results require neither noncompactness nor finite curvature energy. Finally, we construct a complete nonflat critical metric in dimension five with vanishing Cotton tensor, showing that the concircularity and weakly Einstein assumptions are essential in the respective flatness results.

papers.title: Global nonsolvability of the leafwise $\dbar$-equation on foliations with Stein leaves
papers.abstract: Motivated by our previous work on $q$-convexity and global solvability for Levi flat structures, we study the complex foliation associated with the non-tame family of Stein structures constructed by Forstneri\v c and Sigur\dh ard\'ottir. Although every leaf is closed and biholomorphic to $\C^2$ and the foliation admits a complete bundle-like Riemannian metric, there exists a smooth leafwise $\dbar$-closed $(0,1)$-form for which the leafwise $\dbar$-equation admits no global $L^r_{\loc}$ solution for any $0<r\le\infty$. This result also suggests a modification of Questions~2.10.4--2.10.6 in \emph{Foliations: Dynamics, Geometry and Topology}.

papers.title: On a conjecture of Elie Cartan concerning the Gauss equation of a flat submanifold
papers.abstract: We study exteriorly orthogonal (or flat) symmetric bilinear forms on $\R^n$ with values in $\R^p$, continuing the work initiated by \'{E}lie Cartan in 1919 and 1920. In particular, we describe the second fundamental form of an $n$-dimensional flat manifold isometrically immersed in $\E^{n+p}$. Depending on the values of $n$ and $p$, Cartan's results either can be extended to this setting or fail.

papers.title: The Schoen-Yau-Schick Obstruction in All Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that closed Schoen--Yau--Schick manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature in all dimensions. Building on the singular dimension descent of Bi--Zhu, we extend their topological argument from overtorical manifolds to the Schoen--Yau--Schick setting. The key is to detect a non-spherical two-dimensional homology class by a cohomology class with finite coefficients and preserve the resulting nonzero degree throughout the descent, leading to a contradiction on the terminal surface.

papers.title: (Non-)existence of complex structures on $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper we determine which $8$-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent real Lie algebras admit (integrable) complex structures. We construct explicit examples on $40$ out of the $43$ isomorphism classes, and show that there are obstructions to the existence of complex structures on the remaining three isomorphism classes. These obstructions are related to the set of elements of rank $2$ in the pencil defining the Lie algebra structure. We also show that for any even-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$, the direct sum $\mathfrak{g}:=\mathbb{R}^2\oplus \mathfrak{h}$ (and also some other, more general, extensions of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by $\mathfrak{h}$) admits a complex structure if and only if $\mathfrak{h}$ admits a complex structure. In particular, this allows us to construct the first examples of $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras in every even dimension $2n\geq8$ which do not admit complex structures. Finally, we show that every even-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebra with $2$-dimensional center admits a complex structure.

papers.title: A Trajectory-Based Mathematical Framework for Wildfire Front Propagation in Heterogeneous Landscapes
papers.abstract: We present a mathematical formulation based on trajectories for modeling the propagation of wildfire fronts in heterogeneous landscapes and apply it to the Brazilian Pantanal. The formulation is made up of a direction-dependent propagation law and Finsler orthogonality along a moving boundary. This results in a nonlinear local system for outward fire front trajectories. We provide a strictly convex translated ellipse representation at each point of the evolving boundary which guaranties uniqueness and existence of the chosen outward velocity. The effective propagation coefficients that are dependent on space and the hourly wind forcing permit the perimeter to evolve irregularly without imposing a fixed global front geometry. Computed trajectories were georeferenced and isotropically spatially registered with VIIRS active-fire observations. ERA5 wind and ERA5-Land vegetation data were used to describe the environmental forcing and landscape heterogeneity. The full-run Dice coefficients for the observation-guided spatial comparisons for the exploratory experiments for September 3-5, 2020 are 0.578, 0.571, and 0.467 respectively. One-at-a-time sensitivity perturbations of the spatial propagation coefficient, wind speed magnitude and rate-law exponents quantify the governing influence of the environmental forcing and parameter variations on the spatial extent of the calculated fire advance. These observed patterns also guided calibration and, in the absence of exact timestamps of satellite acquisition, the results show within-event spatial agreement rather than independent predictive validation. The framework provides a mathematically rigorous basis for subsequent uncertainty quantification, independent validation over multiple events and prospective sector-wise assessments of simulated fire spread.

papers.title: Quaternionic Torus Actions on Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study smooth actions of quaternionic tori $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$ on closed, connected smooth manifolds, establishing sharp bounds for $r$ in terms of the dimension of the manifold when the action is either effective, effective almost-free, or almost-effective. In particular, we prove that an almost-effective $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$-action on an $n$-dimensional manifold satisfies $r\leq \lfloor2n/3\rfloor$, and we classify up to diffeomorphism all simply connected manifolds attaining the maximal possible rank. This gives a quaternionic counterpart of the maximal symmetry rank conjecture without any curvature assumption. We also establish the bounds $r\leq n/3$ for effective and effective almost-free quaternionic torus actions, and we compute the exact value for spheres, quoric manifolds, or manifolds of the form $(S^3)^a\times (S^1)^b$.

papers.title: Volume growth and gap Theorem for manifolds with non-negative complex sectional curvature
papers.abstract: The combined work of Liu, Ni, and Ni-Tam established that a complete K\"ahler manifold with positive bisectional curvature has Euclidean volume growth if and only if its curvature decays quadratically on average. In this work, we use the approximation scheme developed by Cabezas-Rivas and Wilking to establish the Riemannian analogue under the assumption of nonnegative complex sectional curvature. As an application, we prove an optimal gap theorem for manifolds with nonnegative complex sectional curvature. These results generalize the authors' earlier work.

papers.title: Gravitational Illumination Bodies
papers.abstract: For a given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R ^n$ and $\delta>0$, we introduce a new class of bodies, the {\em gravitational illumination bodies} $I^\delta(K)$. We show some of their properties and explore their relation to floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. Unexpected phenomena happen and the gravitational illumination bodies exhibit very different behavior than the floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. While the classical bodies are all convex and either contained in $K$ or containing $K$, this is no longer the case for the new bodies. They need not be convex, but they are star shaped and it may happen that $I^\delta(K)$ has non-empty intersection with both, $K$ and its complement. Moreover, the containment behavior may change with the dimension. Most surprising is the behavior of a volume derivative, $$ \lim_{\delta \to 0} \frac{ |\vol_n(K)-\vol_n(I^\delta(K)) |}{\delta^\frac{2}{n+1}}. $$ In all dimensions the corresponding volume derivative for the classical bodies results in the equi-affine invariant affine surface area of the body $K$. In the case of the gravitational illumination body, this is also the case in all dimensions, except in dimension $3$. In dimension $3$ the limit is equal to $0$ for all convex bodies. A non-zero derivative is obtained in dimension $3$ if one normalizes by $\delta$ instead of $\delta^\frac{1}{2}$. The non-zero limit is a new affine invariant involving the {\em affine mean curvature } and the {\em Pick invariant} of the convex body.

papers.title: Einstein Constants and Smooth Topology, Revisited
papers.abstract: In 1997, Catanese and the first author showed that, for every $m\geq 2$, there exists a smooth closed $4m$-manifold that admits both a $\lambda > 0$ Einstein metric and a $\lambda < 0$ Einstein metric; thus, the sign of the Einstein constant $\lambda$ is not always determined by the differential topology of the host compact manifold. This result was later improved by R\u{a}sdeaconu and \c{S}uvaina (2009), who showed that there are in fact at least $\binom{m + 3}{3}$ topologically distinct such examples in each dimension $4m$, $m\geq 2$. In this note, we further improve these earlier results by showing that infinitely many topologically distinct examples of this phenomenon actually occur in dimension $4m$, for each $m\geq 2$.

papers.title: Invariant solitons of the inverse mean curvature flow in the sphere and in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We study hypersurfaces of the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ and of hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, $n\ge 3$, that move under the inverse mean curvature flow by a one-parameter group of isometries. No closed hypersurface has this property, and a soliton with constant mean curvature is an open subset of a horosphere. For the rotation hypersurfaces of do Carmo and Dajczer, of spherical, hyperbolic and parabolic type, the soliton equation reduces to a single ordinary differential equation, which we analyse in every dimension. In $\mathbb{H}^n$ the horosphere appears at the critical speed $\lambda=1$ and separates entire bowls from solitons that end at a singular $(n-2)$-sphere; each class has exactly one horospherical end, and it is the threshold between ends asymptotic to totally geodesic hypersurfaces and ends at a singular orbit. At an axis of codimension two we obtain a complete trichotomy, which changes at the speed $\lambda=2(n-1)$ from logarithmic spirals to cuspidal edges. In $\mathbb{S}^n$ no rotational soliton through the axis is complete, and the radius of its singular sphere satisfies $\frac{\pi}{2}-r_+=\frac{K_n}{\lambda}\left(1-2(n-1)^2\lambda^{-2}\log\lambda\right)+O(\lambda^{-3})$, with $K_n=\sqrt{\pi}\,\Gamma(\frac{n+1}{2})/\Gamma(\frac{n}{2})$. For $n=3$, the commuting pairs of Killing fields give two further classes, helicoidal and Hopf-invariant surfaces; the latter are the rotators of the inverse curve shortening flow on the round two-sphere.
